text:
incident-bot: P0 detected: elevated inference errors (502/timeout) from region az-east-1a. Error rate spike 06:12 UTC. Auto-mitigation not triggered. Paging oncall

sam: seeing 502s from the inference fleet, many client TCP resets. Grafana: 95p latency up from 120ms -> 2s, error rate 6%. Requesting immediate assessment.

jordana: logs show repeated ENETUNREACH/connection reset on g5 nodes in az-east-1a, kernel reprobes around NIC RX ring. Also kvcache miss rate increasing — suggests stuck workers.

marta: I'm oncall, taking it. marking incident P0. starting investigation. @pagerduty escalate to infra team.

pagerduty: marta acknowledged the page and pinged infra-sre.

sam: quick customer-impact calc: ~8% of requests for hosted API from this region are failing, global fallback to other AZs mitigates ~65% but tail latency for affected customers hitting pinned dedicated pools is high.

jordana: confirmed some dedicated capacity pools pinned to az-east-1a are saturated/partially unreachable. AWS console shows multiple ENI resets and host network degraded. No control-plane API issues yet.

marta: immediate plan: 1) stop scheduling new inference tasks to az-east-1a 2) drain warm workers gracefully 3) increase cross-AZ burst capacity and open cross-region fallback for critical customers 4) keep TTL low for DNS so clients pick up new endpoints fast.

sam: commands I'm running now:
```
# mark az-east-1a as degraded
redwood infra region set-health --region az-east-1 --zone a --status degraded --ticket 1799004321
# scale up az-east-1b pools
redwood infra pool adjust --region az-east-1 --zone b --pool inference-hosted --scale +40
```

jordana: starting graceful drain: `redwood runtime drain --zone az-east-1a --max-wait 90s` — will preserve kv cache when possible. but expect some cold-starts.

marta: @sam confirm we can lower DNS TTL for the api hostname? want clients to respect new endpoints quickly.

sam: lowering TTL to 30s via infra DNS API now.

incident-bot: postmortem checklist created: /incidents/1799004321/checklist. added runbook entries executed by oncall.

leo: I'm taking the oncall handoff to coordinate with AWS. sending a support case to AWS NLB/ENI team, attaching ENI logs and instance ids.

marta: update for customer success: some customers on pinned dedicated pools are seeing failed requests ~10-12% depending on routing. Most hosted customers unaffected due to cross-AZ failover. CS contact prepared a canned message.

cs-rep: drafted message: "We're seeing degraded inference performance affecting some workloads in az-east-1a; we've rerouted traffic and are working with infra to restore full capacity. No data exposure. ETA unknown, will update in 30m."

jordana: note: kvcache stall symptom — when we failed over some traffic, we saw larger-than-usual KV reloads causing temporary backlog. watch for token-cost spike.

sam: mitigation status: 1) new scheduling blocked to a1a — DONE. 2) drain started — in progress (30% drained). 3) az-east-1b scaled +45% — instances coming up. 4) DNS TTL lowered — DONE. 5) cross-region fallback for critical customers enabled to eu-west-1 if both AZs in region fail - staged.

marta: handing to leo for AWS coordination and longer-term recovery. I'm staying in channel for customer comms.

leo: AWS support responded: "We see host-level network flapping in AZ a causing ENI resets. We're investigating fabric layer on our side." Requested instance-level connectivity test and host replacement.

jordana: started rolling replacement of affected host instances in az-east-1a to force AWS to move pods: `redwood infra host replace --zone az-east-1a --filter 'g5' --parallel 8`

sam: telemetry shows error-rate dropping to 3% after initial draining and scale up; 95p latency for region down to 420ms. still above SLO but improving.

incident-bot: incident update (06:35 UTC): status: mitigation in progress, impact reduced.

leo: AWS confirmed noisy host pool; they will evacuate and reprovision capacity. ETA unknown but they prioritized. We asked for replacement rate and confirmation when NLB healthchecks return to normal.

marta: next steps: keep DNS TTL low for one hour, continue draining until healthy, monitor kv miss/cold start cost. Prepare post-incident follow-up: customer list, error breakdown, regen billing adjustments if needed.

cs-rep: will send initial customer note in 10m with current mitigation steps and expected next update at +30m.

sam: logging note for postmortem: "root cause appears to be host-level network flapping in az-east-1a causing ENI resets and stuck inference workers leading to kvcache churn and client timeouts; mitigations were traffic draining, AZ scale-up, DNS TTL change, and host replacements."

marta: handing off to leo (oncall) at 06:40 UTC. marking channel read-only for other non-essential chatter so we can keep timeline clear. reactions only. :lock:

leo: taking over. I'll keep this channel updated with AWS progress and recovery metrics. if we see error rate >4% after 30m we escalate to cross-region failover for more customers.

incident-bot: final note appended to thread: timeline saved, runbook executed steps recorded.

marta: thanks team, standing by for post-incident review.
